alt.en: A printed magazine page in two columns, headed "Brown's Book-Stall", page 7. The left column ends a paragraph of text and prints a song headed "Bonnie Loch Loman" in seven verses with a chorus, with the imprint "Published by Paterson & Roy, 27 George Street, Edinburgh" at its foot. The right column prints a second song in seven short verses between paragraphs of text.
alt.es: Página impresa de una revista a dos columnas, con el encabezado "Brown's Book-Stall", página 7. La columna izquierda termina un párrafo de texto e imprime una canción titulada "Bonnie Loch Loman" en siete estrofas con estribillo, con el pie de imprenta "Published by Paterson & Roy, 27 George Street, Edinburgh" al final. La columna derecha imprime una segunda canción en siete estrofas breves entre párrafos de texto.

caption.en: The earliest known text of the song, the Edinburgh sheet Bonnie Loch Loman of about 1840, as Brown's Book-Stall of Aberdeen reprinted it in December 1911, beside the verses Lady John Scott said she picked up from a boy singing in the streets.
caption.es: El texto más antiguo que se conoce de la canción, la hoja de Edimburgo Bonnie Loch Loman de hacia 1840, tal como la reimprimió Brown's Book-Stall, de Aberdeen, en diciembre de 1911, junto a las estrofas que Lady John Scott dijo haber recogido de un niño que cantaba por las calles.

source: "About Some 'Auld Sangs'", Brown's Book-Stall, No. 75 (Aberdeen: A. Brown & Co., December 1911), p. 7, reprinting "Bonnie Loch Loman" (Paterson & Roy, Edinburgh, about 1840)
library: University of Guelph Library (digitized by the Internet Archive)
callNumber: DA 890.A2 B7 v. 2; Internet Archive brownsbookstalln02aber, image n666
licenceEvidence: Published Aberdeen, December 1911 (masthead "No. 75. December. 1911."); unsigned article, the quoted collector Gavin Greig died 1914; the reprinted sheet is of about 1840. Internet Archive record: "possible-copyright-status: In the Public Domain". Faithful scan of a flat page adds no new copyright (see rights.md).
credit: University of Guelph Library, via the Internet Archive

alt.en: A page of printed music, page 10, headed "Loch Lomond", marked "Old Scottish Song" at the left and "Traditional Melody arranged by Malcolm Lawson" at the right. A voice line with three verses of words runs above a piano part, under the direction "With much feeling and rather slow".
alt.es: Página de música impresa, página 10, con el encabezado "Loch Lomond", y las indicaciones "Old Scottish Song" a la izquierda y "Traditional Melody arranged by Malcolm Lawson" a la derecha. Una línea de voz con tres estrofas de letra va sobre una parte de piano, bajo la indicación "With much feeling and rather slow".

caption.en: Loch Lomond as Songs of the North prints it, an "Old Scottish Song" with the traditional melody arranged by Malcolm Lawson: the earliest printing with this tune that we have seen, in a book first published in London in 1885.
caption.es: Loch Lomond tal como la imprime Songs of the North, una "Old Scottish Song" (vieja canción escocesa) con la melodía tradicional en arreglo de Malcolm Lawson: la impresión más antigua con esta melodía que hemos visto, en un libro publicado por primera vez en Londres en 1885.

source: A. C. Macleod and Harold Boulton, editors, music arranged by Malcolm Lawson, Songs of the North, vol. I (London: J. B. Cramer & Co., undated later printing; first published by Field and Tuer, 1885), "Loch Lomond", p. 10
library: University of Toronto, Faculty of Music Library (digitized by the Internet Archive)
callNumber: M1746 B78 S6 19--, barcode 31761034118778; Internet Archive 31761034118778, image n29
licenceEvidence: Work first published 1885 (Field and Tuer, London); this copy an undated later Cramer printing of the same pages. Arranger Malcolm Lawson died 1918; editors Anne Campbell Macleod (Lady Wilson) died 1921 and Harold Boulton died 1935; the words are an anonymous "Old Scottish Song". Faithful scan of a flat page adds no new copyright (see rights.md).
credit: University of Toronto, Faculty of Music Library, via the Internet Archive

alt.en: A sepia photograph across still water to a wooded shore, with a white two-storey house among the trees, a thin spit of land with two small trees in the water in front, and bare rounded hills rising behind into a long valley. White lettering along the bottom reads "Camstraddan House and Glen Luss from Inchtavannach, Loch Lomond. 1210. G.W.W."
alt.es: Fotografía en sepia que mira, sobre el agua en calma, hacia una orilla con árboles, con una casa blanca de dos plantas entre ellos, una lengua de tierra estrecha con dos arbolillos en el agua delante y, detrás, colinas redondeadas y peladas que se abren en un valle largo. Unas letras blancas al pie dicen "Camstraddan House and Glen Luss from Inchtavannach, Loch Lomond. 1210. G.W.W."

caption.en: The west bank of Loch Lomond at Luss, with Glen Luss behind, photographed by George Washington Wilson of Aberdeen between about 1865 and 1880; the song's first verse looks back on walks along the loch's banks and braes.
caption.es: La orilla oeste del Loch Lomond en Luss, con Glen Luss detrás, fotografiada por George Washington Wilson, de Aberdeen, entre 1865 y 1880 aproximadamente; la primera estrofa de la canción recuerda los paseos por las orillas y laderas (banks and braes) del lago.

source: George Washington Wilson, "Camstraddan House and Glen Luss from Inchtavannach, Loch Lomond" (title on object), albumen print in an album; cropped to the print
licenceEvidence: Rijksmuseum object page: Copyright "Public domain", linked to the Creative Commons Public Domain Mark 1.0 (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/); data record rights https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/. Photograph made 1865 to 1880; George Washington Wilson died 1893 (see rights.md).
credit: Rijksmuseum, Amsterdam, RP-F-00-5359-17, gift of W. Diepraam, Amsterdam

alt.en: A sepia photograph from a height over a wide loch, with dark fir trees along the bottom edge, a small wooded island in the middle of the water, a wooded point reaching out from the left, and a broad mountain rising from the far shore at the right. White lettering at the bottom reads "Ben Lomond and Loch Lomond from Inchtavannach. 1207. G.W.W."
alt.es: Fotografía en sepia tomada desde lo alto sobre un lago ancho, con abetos oscuros a lo largo del borde inferior, una islita con árboles en medio del agua, una punta de tierra arbolada que sale desde la izquierda y una montaña ancha que se alza en la otra orilla, a la derecha. Unas letras blancas al pie dicen "Ben Lomond and Loch Lomond from Inchtavannach. 1207. G.W.W."

caption.en: Ben Lomond above Loch Lomond, photographed from Inchtavannach by George Washington Wilson between about 1865 and 1880; in the second verse the lovers parted "on the steep, steep side o' Ben Lomon'".
caption.es: El Ben Lomond sobre el Loch Lomond, fotografiado desde Inchtavannach por George Washington Wilson entre 1865 y 1880 aproximadamente; en la segunda estrofa, los enamorados se separaron "on the steep, steep side o' Ben Lomon'" (en la empinada ladera del Ben Lomond).

source: George Washington Wilson, "Ben Lomond and Loch Lomond from Inchtavannach" (title on object), albumen print in an album; cropped to the print
